title: Stormers balance URC ambitions with Springbok hopes against Ulster
text: Stormers balance URC ambitions with Springbok hopes against Ulster With Springbok debuts potentially on the horizon, John Dobson has challenged the Stormers’ young Bok hopefuls to put Ulster first as the Cape side look to preserve their unbeaten home record. Stormers utility forward Riley Norton will look to put in a big shift off the bench in the URC clash against Ulster ahead of his first senior Springbok tour in the Nations Championship.latest crop of Springbok squad members will have to strike a delicate balance between helping their club maintain their unbeaten home start to the, knowing that another victory would strengthen their early-season position before the international break. They currently occupy fourth spot on the official URC log.against Italy, France and Ireland present an added layer of motivation for several young players hoping to catch the eye of Springbok coach Rassie Erasmus. Stormers director of rugby John Dobson acknowledged that managing a growing number of Springboks was becoming increasingly challenging. But, he is also chuffed to see the success of the Cape franchise’s player-development pathway.Centre Markus Muller, flyhalf Yaqeen Ahmed and utility forward Riley Norton are the latest youngsters to make it into the Bok touring squad.“We always want to find a fine line between having a lot of Springboks and, you know, I think we’ve been sitting quite nicely in the middle,” Dobson said. “But having so many players away is not ideal for our campaign. I suppose it’s a consequence of your own success. We want to bring these youngsters through, expose them, and then they become Springboks.It’s not an overwhelmingly comfortable number in terms of managing the home situation here.“It’s a lot of players touring, but at the same time it’s fantastic for our project. You want to become a Springbok? Come to the Stormers. They’re going to give you your opportunities, and that narrative is super important for us.” With the Springboks potentially playing in the Nations Championship final on 29 November, the Stormers could face a difficult turnaround before their next URC fixture against the Sharks the following Saturday. Dobson admitted that expecting players to celebrate a possible international triumph, return home and immediately prepare for club duty would be a significant ask.During the international break, Dobson and his coaches will make plans for any eventuality should they be without a handful of players for that derby at Kings Park.“It’s going to present some challenges, especially if, God willing, the Springboks play in the Nations Championship final on 29 November. We play the Sharks the following Saturday, and I don’t think you can expect too many Springboks to win that final, celebrate, get back, train and then play for us the next Saturday. So it is a lot for us at the moment,” he said.Dobson added that the Stormers players were eager to make their mark in the final clash, particularly with places up for grabs over the next couple of Tests.“Obviously, Markus isn’t playing this week, but I think the rest are young and want to impress and stake a claim to play against Italy or be on the tour. They’re not going to do that by protecting themselves against Ulster.“It’s not an easy situation for the players because as soon as you go into a game not wanting to get injured, that’s when you get injured. So, it is a challenge. We heard the rumours earlier this week about their inclusion but nothing was confirmed. I never never expected it, but I think it’s really progressive for South African rugby.” The immediate priority remains Ulster. With the Stormers keen to maintain their unbeaten home record, their youngsters must first deliver for their club before turning their attention to the prospect of wearing the green and gold.
